'''''Euphorbia heptagona''''', sometimes referred to as the '''milk barrel''' or '''pincushion euphorbia''', is a subtropical [[succulent plant|succulent]] [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the genus ''[[Euphorbia]]'' native to [[South Africa]].  The species is also grown as a [[houseplant]].{{Cn|date=February 2025}}

== Description ==
''Euphorbia heptagona'' forms dense clusters of small succulent branches. Each branch typically has four ridges, each with a line of long spines.{{Cn|date=February 2025}} Young spines are often red or yellow, darkening to black as they mature.<ref name="Brown1916">{{cite journal |author=Brown |first=N. E. |year=1916 |title=Two Little-Known South African Euphorbias |url=https://ia800607.us.archive.org/view_archive.php?archive=/8/items/crossref-pre-1923-scholarly-works/10.2307%252F4118579.zip&file=10.2307%252F4119519.pdf |journal=[[Bulletin of Miscellaneous Information]] |volume=1916 |issue=3 |access-date=18 February 2025 |page=44}}</ref> Like all Euphorbia species, ''Euphorbia heptagona'' exudes toxic white latex when damaged.<ref name="Kgosiemang2025">{{Cite journal |last1=Kgosiemang |first1=Ipeleng Kopano Rosinah |last2=Lefojane |first2=Relebohile |last3=Adegoke |first3=Ayodeji Mathias |last4=Ogunyemi |first4=Oludare |last5=Mashele |first5=Samson Sitheni |last6=Sekhoacha |first6=Mamello Patience |date=January 2025 |title=Pharmacological Significance, Medicinal Use, and Toxicity of Extracted and Isolated Compounds from Euphorbia Species Found in Southern Africa: A Review |journal=Plants |language=en |volume=14 |issue=3 |pages=469 |doi=10.3390/plants14030469 |issn=2223-7747 |pmc=11821031 |pmid=39943031 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

''Euphorbia heptagona'' closely resembles many [[Cactus|cacti]], but this resemblance is due to [[Convergent evolution|convergent evolution]]. Euphorbias are not closely related to cacti.

Tests on the plant have identified the presence of [[Flavonoid|flavonoids]], [[alkaloids]], [[Tannin|tannins]], [[Glycoside|glycosides]], [[anthraquinones]], [[triterpenoids]], and [[Phytosterol|phytosterols]].<ref name="Kgosiemang2025" />

== Taxonomy ==
The species was named ''Euphorbia heptagona'' in 1753 by [[Carl Linnaeus]]. It is classified in the genus ''[[Euphorbia]]'' as part of the [[Euphorbiaceae]] family. It has twelve [[heterotypic synonym]]s several [[Variety (botany)|varieties]], but no accepted varieties.<ref name="POWO">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=346763-1 |title=''Euphorbia heptagona'' L. |access-date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

== Names ==
''Euphorbia heptagona'' is known by the [[common name]] ''milk barrel''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Smith |first1=Gideon |last2=Van Wyk |first2=Ben-Erik |title=The Garden Succulents Primer |date=2008 |publisher=Timber Press |location=Portland, Oregon |isbn=978-0-88192-954-6 |page=172 |url=https://archive.org/details/gardensucculents0000smit |access-date=29 May 2026}}</ref>

== Habitat ==
Native to South Africa, ''Euphorbia heptagona'' commonly grows in the [[Eastern Cape]] and [[Karoo]] regions.<ref name="Kgosiemang2025" /> 

It grows best in well-drained soil and with direct sunlight.<ref name="Kgosiemang2025" />
